History and Physical (H&P – Super Detailed)

Consult Summary:
73-year-old man with known chronic heart failure presents with 2-week progressive dyspnea, worsening markedly over the last few days, associated with new bilateral ankle swelling and mild dry cough; clinical impression is acute decompensation of chronic heart failure—plan to increase loop diuretic, obtain blood work and echocardiogram, and review in one week.

History:
• Presenting complaint – Shortness of breath.  
• Onset/duration – Gradual over ≈2 weeks; markedly worse past 2–3 days.  
• Course/progression – Previously able to walk to shops; now must stop and rest and is breathless doing household activities.  
• Associated symptoms – Mild dry cough; bilateral ankle swelling noted over same recent days; feels “a little run-down.”  
• Denied symptoms – Chest pain, palpitations, fever/temperature, chills, sputum production, dizziness, syncope, appetite change, urinary difficulty (passes urine frequently as usual).  
• Exacerbating/relieving factors – None specifically reported; no mention of positional change, medications, or activity that clearly improves symptoms.  
• Review of systems (pertinent negatives/positives) – No wheeze, no orthostatic symptoms; no alcohol intake; ex-smoker. No other systemic complaints recorded.

Past Medical History:
• Chronic heart failure – On loop diuretic; prior similar episode with ankle swelling.  
• Remote myocardial infarction (“small heart attack”) ≈5 years ago; brief hospitalization, recovered.  
• No other chronic illnesses reported.

Current Medications:
• Furosemide – “one tablet daily,” exact dose/route/frequency not documented; plan to increase to one tablet twice daily.  
• Aspirin – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• Bisoprolol – dose/route/frequency not documented.

Drug Allergies:
• No known drug allergies.

Social History:
• Lives alone with two cats (Polly and Tim).  
• Employment – Part-time lorry (truck) driver; daytime shifts only; notes work is physically tiring.  
• Smoking – Former smoker; ~1 pack/day for 25 years; quit (year not specified).  
• Alcohol – Denies alcohol use.  
• Recreational drugs – Not discussed.  
• Exercise – Limited to walking to the shops daily; no strenuous exercise.

Family History:
• Father – Died of heart attack in early 60s.  
• Mother – Living; osteoporosis.  
• No other hereditary conditions noted.

Physical Examination:
(Exact vitals not provided; clinician stated they were “OK.”)  
• General – Appears stable per clinician.  
• Chest/Respiratory – “Chest examination OK” per clinician (no wheeze/crackles reported).  
• Cardiovascular – Blood pressure reported “OK” (numeric values not given); no palpitations.  
• Extremities – Bilateral ankle edema reported by patient (extent not quantified).  
• Oxygen saturation – Reported as “OK” (value not documented).

Investigations:
• Planned – Blood tests (CBC to assess anemia, renal function, others as appropriate).  
• Planned – Echocardiogram to assess current cardiac function.  
• None performed during consultation; no prior results provided.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Acute decompensated chronic heart failure (likely volume overload).  
• Plan:  
  – Increase Furosemide from 1 tablet daily to 1 tablet twice daily for several days.  
  – Order blood work (CBC, renal profile, ± BNP per standard protocols).  
  – Arrange outpatient echocardiogram within 1–2 weeks.  
  – Review in clinic/tele-visit in 1 week to reassess symptoms, weight, edema, renal function.  
  – Educate patient to seek earlier care if dyspnea worsens, chest pain, palpitations, dizziness, or other concerning symptoms occur.

Issue 2: Monitor for potential precipitating factors (infection, ischemia, pulmonary embolism).  
• Plan:  
  – Counsel patient on watching for fever, productive cough, chest discomfort.  
  – Consider additional work-up if new symptoms develop (e.g., chest X-ray, ECG, troponin).

Issue 3: Cardiovascular risk and lifestyle management.  
• Plan:  
  – Reinforce smoking cessation maintenance; no alcohol—commend adherence.  
  – Encourage gradual physical activity as tolerated; monitor symptoms.  
  – Discuss occupational considerations if symptoms limit driving; revisit at follow-up.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
1. Acute decompensated (congestive) heart failure – High likelihood; known HF, classic exertional dyspnea plus peripheral edema, improvement expected with diuretic uptitration.  
2. Lower-respiratory tract infection precipitating HF flare – Moderate likelihood; dry cough and fatigue could indicate viral bronchitis; afebrile and clear chest exam lower probability.  
3. Pulmonary embolism – Low–moderate likelihood; sedentary occupation is a risk factor, but symptom progression was subacute and lacks pleuritic pain or unilateral leg swelling.

Quality checks (document_quality):
• Missing elements – Exact vitals (BP, HR, RR, SpO₂), weight, orthopnea/PND history, full medication doses/frequencies, allergy reconciliation beyond drugs (foods/latex), vaccination status.  
• Transcript/DDx conflicts – None significant; DDx aligns with transcript.  
• Transcript quality – Generally clear; occasional audio dropouts (e.g., difficulty hearing Bisoprolol); no major data loss.
